title: FTSE Russell December 2026 reconstitution lock-down begins — the first December reconstitution lock-down, and the owner publishes the date outright
source: EST: OWNER-PUBLISHED, not rule-derived -- this is the correction this event's own initial research makes to the proposal that carried the id. FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions -- Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents PDF, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 content streams inflated and text-extracted in-session 2026-09-06; the cover reads "lseg.com/en/ftse-russell July 2026 ... Frequently Asked Questions" and seven page footers read back "Russell US Equity Indexes, July 2026"). Its dated four-column schedule table -- Quarterly IPO March 2026 | Semi-Annual Reconstitution June 2026 | Quarterly IPO September 2026 | Semi-Annual Reconstitution December 2026 -- carries the row "Lock-Down Period (open of)" with the values "9 March 2026 | 8 June 2026 | 7 September 2026 | 30 NOVEMBER 2026". The December value IS this date, stated by the index owner. The same table publishes the December "Query Period (window for clients to query the data visible within the files)" as "16 November 2026 to 27 November 2026", which the proposal had derived rather than read. The June value, 8 June 2026, matches the lock-down date FTSE Russell's own 2026 schedule press release published, which is the internal check on the table. THE RULE IS ALSO STATED VERBATIM in the same document: "A lockdown period applies ahead of each implementation. For the June review, the lockdown begins on the Monday at the open, three weeks prior to implementation. For the December review, the lockdown begins on the Monday at the open, two weeks prior to implementation. From the start of the lockdown period, index review changes are considered final." Implementation is Friday 2026-12-11 (tracked as russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 and stated verbatim by the owner's reconstitution page), and the two trading weeks ending on it are 11-30..12-04 and 12-07..12-11 -- first day Monday 2026-11-30. CORROBORATED by ground rules v7.2, August 2026 (lseg.com dam PDF, HTTP 200, 746,491 bytes, 77 content streams inflated in-session 2026-09-06), Appendix F's DECEMBER column: Query Period "For two weeks following preliminary announcement", Lock down "Two weeks after query period ends", Implementation "2nd Friday of December" -- the query period ends Friday 2026-11-27 and the two weeks after begin Monday 2026-11-30. Three sources, one date. WHY IT REMAINS estimate, and the reason has changed: NOT because no owner schedule names it (the proposal's premise, refuted above) but because this calendar's confirmed-tier source prefixes have no member for an index owner's own published schedule -- the identical prefix gap the russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 and russell-recon-preliminary-2026-11-13 ledgers both banked -- and because the FAQ table carries the owner's own caveat verbatim: "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes." Promote when a prefix for an index owner exists. Canonical file written by this event's own never-assessed initial research 2026-09-06, superseding proposals/russell-recon-lockdown-2026-11-30.from-russell-recon-lockdown-2027-06-07.json (read in full first)
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-06); the id existed only as the proposal named above, which was read in full first and whose findings are carried forward except where measured against. THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE PROPOSAL, all sourced. (1) The date is owner-published, not rule-derived -- see source. (2) "The FIRST December lock-down in the index family's history" is true only of RECONSTITUTION lock-downs: the same FAQ table shows lock-down periods already running for the quarterly IPO reviews at 9 March 2026 and 7 September 2026, so a lock-down boundary is routine and only the December reconstitution leg is new. (3) 2026-09-07, an owner-published "Lock-Down Period (open of)" date, IS LABOR DAY -- a full US market holiday -- which shows the "at the open" boundary is an index-administration boundary, not a trading-session one; that refines the sibling ledger's reading of ground-rules 6.4.1, which treated it as a session boundary. THE MEASURED HEADLINE, and it is why this entry now says something the proposal did not: 2026-11-30 IS NOT A PLACEBO. The sibling registered this date as the out-of-sample test of a June result whose whole value was being an empty date (June lock-down Mondays: IWM-vs-SPY +0.013% mean, p=45.3%, n=7). But the calendar slot 2026-11-30 occupies -- the Monday after Thanksgiving -- carries a strong pre-existing small-cap drag with ZERO Russell-December content, since there has never been a December reconstitution: IWM minus SPY on that Monday, 2005-2025, is -0.42% mean, -0.40% median, NEGATIVE IN 18 OF 21 YEARS, one-sided sign p=0.074%, bootstrap p=0.32% against an unconditional -0.00%/session. It survives every control run: not a Monday effect (988 Mondays, -0.02%, 498/988 negative), not a post-holiday effect (193 post-holiday sessions, -0.08%, p=44.3%), not a month-end effect (252 last-business-days, -0.04%, 139/252), stable across sub-periods and STRONGER lately (2016-2025: 10 of 10 negative, -0.58% mean), -0.33% and 17/20 ex-2008. The placebo panel is clean -- shifted by -21/-14/-7/+7/+14/+21 days, no slot clears in the same direction, the inverse of the June panel where two of six empty dates cleared p<0.05. CONSEQUENCE FOR SCORING, registered before the tape rather than argued after it: the confound is roughly 30x the size of the June effect being tested, so any 2026-11-30 day-level read is dominated by the calendar and not by Russell. TWO MORE PRE-REGISTERED BASELINE CORRECTIONS for the sibling's forward tests that score on this date. FT-russell-recon-lockdown-2027-06-07-2 predicts the 2026-11-30 -> 2026-12-11 window prints NEGATIVE; the geometry-matched calendar baseline (lock-down Monday close to second-Friday-of-December close, restricted to the 18 years with 2026's exact 10-session shape) is +0.77% mean, +1.54% median, negative in only 6 of 18 -- so that prediction runs AGAINST the seasonal grain, which makes a negative print strong evidence and a positive print weak disconfirmation. FT-...-1 predicts the lock-down window's mean IWM volume ratio exceeds the query window's; under that test's OWN window definition (prelim close 11-13 -> lock-down close 11-30, vs 11-30 -> implementation 12-11) the calendar-only baseline already steps up in 15 OF 21 YEARS, median +0.069, sign p=3.92% -- so its null is not 50/50 and a bare sign pass is not evidence; score it against a +0.07 step, not against zero. The only non-June lock-down day that has actually traded is 2026-03-09, the quarterly IPO review's: IWM-vs-SPY +0.21% on 1.63x volume, n=1, reported as one observation and nothing more. Impact low and the tier is a call, not an inheritance: the -0.42% drag belongs to the calendar slot, not to the event, no shares move on this date, nothing publishes on it, no house playbook is index-flow-keyed (re-grepped 2026-09-06 for rebalanc|index effect|reconstitution|russell|lock-down|lockdown, zero hits), the implied trade is short IWM against SPY and shorting is blocked house-wide, and symbols is deliberately EMPTY so the deterministic screen cannot trip on small-cap beta. THE CORRIDOR IS HEAVY AND CONFIRMED BY COUNT: 21 tracked events sit within five days, including pce-2026-11-25 and gdp-q3-2026-second-2026-11-25 (both high) at T-3, fomc-blackout-start-2026-11-28 at T-2, chicago-pmi-2026-11-30 / dallas-fed-mfg-2026-11-30 / aws-reinvent-2026 on the day itself, and georgia-senate-runoff-2026-12-01 plus ism-manufacturing-2026-12-01 (both high) at T+1. Kind sector matches the sibling market-structure flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane.
